Limit helper to merge/unite: Clang n32 four-vertex components same +20.7%, root-only +15.2%, copy/groups/query +8.2%; GCC n32 mixed random +3.1% versus control +0.2%.

correctness: All measured same-main outputs exactly matched independent reference tokens; API checksums matched baseline and control. No candidate adopted, so no extra full API correctness claim for rejected alternatives. Main and fast IO kept byte-exact by replacing only body in current pasted submission. Public APIs, union tie rule, ownership and standard fallback unchanged in candidates.

conclusion: No change to production source. Respect small/large and other-operation speed: limited measured improvements did not justify regressions. Results show these specific alternatives are unsuitable; no proof that all further optimizations are impossible.

static_review.task: static review only; no compilation, timing, or production edits
static_review.conclusion: Correct under the existing single-threaded, valid-index invariants. Performance acceptance is outside this static review; the parent reports concrete regressions and rejection of the full candidate.

findings.argument: The first traversal writes only an actually visited vertex and replaces its parent by its old grandparent. If it never visits original b, param[b] stays unchanged and saved pb is its current parent. If it visits original b with a nonroot parent, it changes param[b] to param[pb] and skips pb; the monotonically ascending traversal cannot subsequently visit skipped pb. Thus saved pb remains a strict ancestor, and param[pb] still equals the compressed parent of b. The first b-loop assignment in that case is idempotent, not a reversal of compression. All later b steps have a freshly loaded parent.

The invariant above covers a==b, b on a-path, a on b-path and paths meeting above both vertices. An unchanged root cannot acquire a parent until both finds finish. A negative preloaded pb denotes an initial root, which stays the same root during the first traversal.
The first find cannot alter any entry in the second component; second preloaded parent is fresh. Both returned leaders are unchanged from ordinary finds.
After identical root selection, strict param[a]>param[b] swapping and merge updates are unchanged. Equal-size ties continue to choose the first argument component root.

Union by size still bounds individual path lengths by O(log n). Both traversals retain path halving. Only when the first traversal has already compressed b can the second traversal begin with one idempotent store and one parent hop instead of a halving step; its remaining steps are ordinary halving. There is no downward parent rewrite or unbounded retry, and the claimed inverse-Ackermann amortized behavior is retained. Constant-factor regressions remain possible and must be measured.

The pair holds two ints and allocates nothing. The original vector remains the only owner. Existing bounds checks run for both arguments before any parent loads or writes; valid traversal uses only int assignments and indexed access. Out-of-range exception behavior is unchanged. In SKIP_RUNTIME_CHECKS mode invalid indices continue to violate the API precondition.

Only a private helper and the implementations of merge/same change. Signatures, return types, move/copy behavior, reset, groups and single-leader operations are unchanged. Unspecified internal compression shape is allowed to differ.

test_review.existing_strengths: Reference model checks exact root selection including equal-size merge ties; same vertex, reversed construction, reset/move/copy, all pairs, invalid arguments, allocation and ownership are covered.
test_review.coverage_gap: observe() calls root/leader on vertices before many pair checks and balanced() calls groups() before pair checks, substantially flattening deep paths. Random cases do not guarantee the saved-parent alias case on a fresh deep tree.
test_review.suggestion_if_related_optimization_is_ad: Add one deterministic fresh-tree block for each pair, without root/size/groups/observe calls between tree construction and tested same/merge. Build a 16-vertex balanced tree by unioning adjacent roots at widths 1,2,4,8; pairs (15,15),(15,12),(15,14),(14,15) exercise modified b, ancestor b, modified pb, and opposite order. Verify true same / false redundant merge and representative 0 afterwards. For two disjoint 16-vertex balanced trees, merge deep leaves (15,31) and the reversed pair in separate instances; verify tie leader 0 and 16 respectively, size 32, one component. Existing checked mixed-invalid cases already cover index rejection before the helper.
